role: Lecturer in Physics · University of Ghana
statement: Theoretical nuclear physicist working on the reaction mechanisms that govern the formation of superheavy nuclei, with stochastic dynamics and uncertainty quantification as the principal methods. Teaches undergraduate physics, including PHYS 143, and leads laboratory sessions.

pathways.label: Research
pathways.title: Reaction mechanisms in superheavy element formation
pathways.text: Research on the reaction mechanisms governing the formation of heavy and superheavy nuclei, with emphasis on theoretical modelling, fusion dynamics and fusion–evaporation reactions.

pathways.label: Teaching
pathways.title: Undergraduate physics resources
pathways.text: Slide decks, tutorials, supplementary notes and practice questions for undergraduate physics courses.

pathways.label: Data & Computation
pathways.title: Data science and scientific computing
pathways.text: Data engineering and data science projects, and the scientific computing that supports the research.

selected.title: Fusion Dynamics
selected.text: Revisiting the fusion dynamics in the fusion-by-diffusion model for fusion–evaporation production cross sections.

selected.title: KEWPIE3 Development and Validation
selected.text: Validation of KEWPIE3, the new version of the KEWPIE2 code for fusion–evaporation cross-section predictions in superheavy element synthesis.

selected.title: Uncertainty Analysis of Nuclear Reaction Models
selected.text: Constraining the compound nucleus formation probability in superheavy element synthesis through systematic uncertainty analysis.

selected.title: Superheavy Element Synthesis
selected.text: Theoretical investigation of the reaction mechanisms relevant to the synthesis of heavy and superheavy nuclei, including production cross-sections for Z = 119 and Z = 120.
